newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Hekmatyar to stay away from Afghan talks in north.
newsitem.headline: Hekmatyar to stay away from Afghan talks in north.

text.p: Ousted Afghan prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar supports efforts to forge an anti-Taleban alliance between Uzbek militia leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum and the former government, a spokesman said on Wednesday.
But Ghairat Baheer, designated ambassador to Islamabad by deposed president Burhanuddin Rabbani, said Hekmatyar was unlikely to join current talks between Dostum and Rabbani.
"Hekmatyar is busy with something else, but Rabbani can speak on behalf of the whole government," Baheer said.
Forces of Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami party were fighting alongside those of Rabbani's military chief Ahmad Shah Masood in the Panjsher Valley, northeast of Kabul, and elsewhere, he said.
Several Hezb commanders, including Zardad (one name), Sar Katib and Wahidullah Sabawoon, who was defence minister in the overthrown government, were in the Panjsher Valley, Baheer said.
Baheer, who was unable to present his credentials before the Islamic Taleban militia swept into Kabul on September 27, said Hekmatyar was "in the north", but would not say exactly where.
Rabbani arrived in the northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif, Dostum's headquarters, on Tuesday and embraced Dostum, who split from the government in 1994 after a dispute with Masood.
The Taleban have offered to talk to Dostum, despite his communist past, apparently reluctant to attack him while they are still battling against Masood's forces in the Panjsher Valley.
The Sunni Moslem militants have sworn to impose strict Islamic Sharia law throughout Afghanistan.
"We believe the Taleban cannot go ahead with their programme," Baheer said. "They are not acceptable to the Afghans or to the international community."

The newly-appointed Taleban charge d'affaires at the Afghan embassy in Islamabad, Maulvi Abdul Wahhab, said the Taleban had asked the United Nations to bar Rabbani's deputy foreign minister Abdul Rahim Ghafoorzai from Afghanistan's seat.
"We have sent an official letter to U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali," he said. "Ghafoorzai cannot speak as the representative of Afghanistan. He has been suspended."
